summary: Malaysia grants visa-free entry to most nationalities — 90 days for US, UK, EU and many other passports, 30 days for ASEAN neighbours plus Chinese and Indian citizens under exemptions extended through 2026 — and requires almost all foreign arrivals to submit the free Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) online within 3 days before travel.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on the date of entry into Malaysia.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required only if you arrive from, or transited through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical cover is recommended — private hospitals, which most visitors use, charge in full.

onwardTicket.text: You should hold a confirmed onward or return ticket; immigration officers and airlines may ask for it.

proofOfFunds.text: No official fixed amount is published, but you must be able to show sufficient funds for your stay if asked at the border.

declarations.name: Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC)
declarations.text: Almost all foreign nationals must submit the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival (exemptions cover Singapore citizens using automated lanes, permanent residents and some pass holders). It is free — use only the official Immigration Department portal.

source.name: Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) — official portal

currencyLimits.text: Cash and negotiable bearer instruments exceeding the equivalent of 10,000 USD must be declared on arrival and departure.

notes: Duty-free allowance: 1 litre of alcohol; tobacco products are no longer duty-free at most entry points.
Drug trafficking carries the death penalty under Malaysian law — never carry packages for others.
Alcohol allowances and local rules are stricter in the states of Kelantan and Terengganu.

payments.text: Cards and e-wallets (Touch 'n Go, GrabPay) are accepted widely in cities and malls; hawker stalls, small shops, taxis and rural areas often remain cash-first. ATMs are plentiful and accept foreign cards.

safety.text: Malaysia is generally safe for visitors; petty theft such as bag-snatching occurs in cities. Western governments advise extra caution in the eastern coastal areas of Sabah due to kidnapping risk.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Malaysia Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: Best months depend on the coast: roughly March–September suits the west coast (Penang, Langkawi), while the east coast and its islands are best outside the November–February northeast monsoon.

tips.text: The MDAC arrival card is free. Third-party sites charging a fee for it are unnecessary and often scams — submit it only at imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac within 3 days of arrival.
Malaysia imposes the death penalty for drug trafficking and severe penalties for possession. Never carry luggage or packages for anyone else.
Plan around the monsoons: the east coast islands (Perhentian, Redang, Tioman) largely shut down from November to February, while the west coast stays open year-round.
Sabah and Sarawak (Malaysian Borneo) run their own immigration controls — your passport is checked again when flying there from Peninsular Malaysia, and a separate stay period is stamped.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Malaysia?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders enter Malaysia visa-free for up to 90 days. The only mandatory step is the free Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC), submitted online within 3 days before arrival.

faq.question: What is the MDAC and who needs it?
faq.answer: The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card is a free online arrival form at imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac that almost every foreign visitor must submit within 3 days before arriving. Exemptions cover Singapore citizens using automated lanes, Malaysian permanent residents and holders of certain long-term passes.

faq.question: Can Chinese and Indian citizens visit Malaysia without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Malaysia's visa exemptions for Chinese and Indian citizens allow stays of up to 30 days and have been extended through 31 December 2026. Both still need to submit the free MDAC within 3 days before arrival.

faq.question: How much does a Malaysia eVisa cost?
faq.answer: For the nationalities that need one (including Pakistani and Nigerian citizens), the single-entry tourist eVisa costs roughly 100–200 MYR depending on nationality and where you apply, allows a stay of up to 30 days, and is normally processed within about 48 hours to 5 business days at the official portal malaysiavisa.imi.gov.my.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Malaysia?
faq.answer: It depends on the coast. The west coast (Kuala Lumpur, Penang, Langkawi) is good most of the year, especially around March–September. Avoid the east coast islands between November and February, when the northeast monsoon brings heavy rain and many resorts close.
